original_test_intent: Conditionally change one authorized Chassis indicator to one approved state, confirm the logical and optionally physical effect for a bounded interval, then restore and verify the exact original state without touching other Chassis properties.
original_method: Preserve the Master GET/PATCH conflict and prohibit DeepSeek's assumed payload until the owner confirms the writable representation, property, allowed value and media type; then run one ETag-aware PATCH/readback/observe/restore lifecycle.
manual_activity: The platform/BMC owner resolves the writable `/LED` versus Chassis property representation, approves one target state and visual/service meaning, observation duration, concurrency method, original-state restoration and any human visual correlation.
required_inputs: Corrected testcase or owner ruling on GET versus PATCH
Authorized Chassis and exact writable LED representation
Firmware schema, media type and allowed state vocabulary
One owner-approved target state and bounded duration
Trusted least-privilege write credential and certificate policy
safety_requirements: Do not execute DeepSeek's assumed payload
Do not rely on single-quoted shell text to expand LED_STATE
Do not patch an unadvertised `/LED` child or wrong property
Change exactly one approved field once
Do not mask a real fault indication
Preserve logs and avoid power/reset changes
agent_execution_scope: Bind endpoint and validate writable representation
Validate one target value and exact serialized payload
Collect bounded visual/telemetry evidence if approved
engineer_actions: Resolve source conflict and approve representation/property/value
Approve visible impact, observation and restore plan

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: It must not run as written: the Master defines only GET, `/LED` plus IndicatorLED semantics are unproven, ipmitool is unrelated, `-k`/basic-auth are unsafe, and the single-quoted JSON preserves `${LED_STATE...}` literally rather than expanding it in common shells.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: After owner correction, use trusted secret-safe access to capture original state/ETag, conditionally PATCH exactly one approved indicator property/value with correctly serialized JSON, verify readback/approved observation, then restore and verify the original state.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: The Chassis indicator domain and 15/10 timing remain; endpoint representation, property, value, observation and restore are not inferred.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Model the LED test as a reversible single-property transaction with representation discovery, immutable baseline, concurrency, bounded visible effect and verified restoration.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Prevents a GET-only body and a syntactically non-expanding guessed payload from defining a visible state change.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: The preceding GET can establish logical baseline; this case adds write authorization, transition, observation and restore evidence, but physical LED correctness may still require human or camera confirmation.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: Changing a service indicator can mislead operators or obscure a real fault. Firmware may use OEM values/properties and the write endpoint may differ from the read representation.

project_override_considerations: A Redfish SDK/vendor client is acceptable only after the exact writable contract is approved and when it preserves ETag/concurrency, one-field diff, bounded timing, logical/visual observation and exact restoration evidence.
expected_evidence: Immutable endpoint, trusted certificate and secret-safe write session
Original indicator state, resource identity and ETag/version
Exact serialized one-field PATCH and response/status/new ETag
Post-write readback and bounded logical/visual observation
Exact restore request and final original-state verification

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: The item says PATCH Redfish LED, while the Master Procedure only GETs the LED resource and Criteria assess readability/success. It defines no writable representation/property/value, transition, observation or restoration; DeepSeek's IndicatorLED payload is not authoritative.

blocked_analysis.analysis: The indicator-change domain and reversible workflow are identifiable. An owner/firmware artifact can supply the missing writable contract and target state, so these are concrete prerequisites rather than an irreducible blocker.

review_improvement: Surfaces the GET/PATCH conflict, rejects the non-expanding guessed payload and defines a concurrency-safe, bounded and fully restored indicator transaction.
independent_technical_reasoning: A successful write requires an authoritative writable property and a real serialized target value; the DeepSeek JSON encloses shell expansion syntax in single quotes, so it would commonly send the placeholder literally even before endpoint semantics are considered. Because an indicator communicates operational state, the test must not overwrite a genuine fault or leave a misleading lamp. Capturing state and ETag before the single write, observing the exact transition, and restoring the same original value are necessary to bound both concurrency and operator impact.
